portName: Port of Genoa (Stazioni Marittime: Ponte dei Mille and Ponte Andrea Doria)
seoTitle: Genoa cruise port guide: walk to town, train to Portofino
seoDescription: Genoa cruise port 2026: Principe station 6 min on foot, AMT ticket €2.00 for 110 min, aquarium from €26, bus 782 to Portofino €5.00. Return-time rules.
quickAnswer: Ships dock at the Stazioni Marittime terminals on Ponte dei Mille and Ponte Andrea Doria, about 1 km from the city centre; Genova Piazza Principe station is a 6-minute covered walk. The old town and the aquarium (about 20 minutes, 1.5 km) are walkable, and a €2.00 AMT ticket covers the metro for 110 minutes (2026). For Portofino, take a regional train to Santa Margherita Ligure and AMT bus 782 (€5.00), and be on a train back three hours before all-aboard.
intro: Genoa is a working city rather than a resort, and the cruise terminal sits right on its edge. You can walk off the ship into the medieval lanes (caruggi), the palaces of Via Garibaldi and the Porto Antico waterfront without any transport. The other choice is the Riviera: Portofino by train and bus, or the Cinque Terre, which is possible on a long call but tight. Genoa is also a turnaround port for several lines, so the terminal can be busy with luggage and coaches.

terminals.name: Ponte dei Mille Cruise Terminal
terminals.notes: Run by Stazioni Marittime. About 16,000 m² on three levels linked by escalators and lifts; berths of 340 m and 290 m. Genova Piazza Principe station is a short covered walk.

terminals.name: Ponte Andrea Doria Cruise Terminal
terminals.notes: Run by Stazioni Marittime. About 11,000 m² on two floors with two 300 m berths. Next to Ponte dei Mille; same exits towards Principe and the old town.

walkability.detail: Genova Piazza Principe station is about 6 minutes from the terminal by a lit, covered walkway. The aquarium and Porto Antico are about 20 minutes (1.5 km) on foot along the waterfront. The old town lanes start behind Porto Antico. Genoa is hilly: the caruggi are flat-ish, but anything above Via Garibaldi is steep, and lifts and funiculars help; the Sant'Anna funicular from Piazza Portello is free. The Lanterna lighthouse is reached during the sub-port tunnel works by a shuttle every 20 minutes from Piazzale San Benigno, with tickets reduced to €6 (€5 reduced) while the works last; it has recently opened only at weekends or Friday to Sunday.

transportSections.time: 6 min to Principe station; about 20 min to the aquarium
transportSections.detail: Follow the signs to Principe for the metro and trains, or walk east along the harbour to Porto Antico and the old town.

transportSections.time: About 10 min Principe to San Giorgio (for the aquarium)
transportSections.detail: The metro runs from Principe through Darsena and San Giorgio to De Ferrari and Brignole. The ordinary ticket also covers the Zecca–Righi funicular; the city lifts accept it too. Buy from machines, ticket offices, tabaccherie or the AMT app, and validate at the start of the trip.

transportSections.mode: Regional train to Santa Margherita Ligure (Trenitalia)
transportSections.cost: Distance-based Liguria regional fare; buy in the Trenitalia app or at the machines
transportSections.detail: Trains leave from Genova Piazza Principe and Genova Brignole. Validate paper tickets before boarding. Santa Margherita Ligure–Portofino station is the stop for Portofino.

transportSections.time: Short ride along the coast road
transportSections.detail: The ordinary €2.00 ticket is not valid on this line. Buy the 782 ticket from AMT offices, the app, tabaccherie or machines, and validate it on board. Queues form in Santa Margherita in high season.

Golfo Paradiso runs seasonal boat trips from Genova Porto Antico to Camogli, San Fruttuoso and Portofino, from March into the autumn, subject to weather. From Santa Margherita, Traghetti Portofino (Servizio Marittimo del Tigullio) Line 1 links Santa Margherita, Portofino and San Fruttuoso; tickets are sold only at the boarding point and sailings need at least 20 passengers.

transportSections.cost: Liguria fare plus a Cinque Terre supplement of €3, €5 or €6 by day category (2026)
transportSections.time: Just under an hour to Monterosso on the fastest trains; longer on regionals
transportSections.detail: Between Levanto and La Spezia, non-Liguria residents pay the special Cinque Terre fare (€5, €8 or €10 per single trip, valid 75 minutes) from 14 March to 1 November 2026. Only realistic on a long call.

returnTiming.rule: From Portofino, be on a train out of Santa Margherita at least 3 hours before all-aboard (14:30 for a 17:30 all-aboard). From the old town or the aquarium, start walking back 75 minutes before.
returnTiming.detail: Allow for the 782 bus queue or boat timetable, a train of up to an hour, the walk from Principe, and 90 minutes on board before all-aboard because the return depends on a train. From the aquarium the walk is about 20 minutes, or take the metro from San Giorgio to Principe.
returnTiming.emergencyFallback: If a train is cancelled, take the next regional or Intercity to Piazza Principe; Brignole also connects to Principe by metro. In the city, a taxi to the terminal is short. Call the port agent number in your daily programme if you might be late.

excursionAdvice: Genoa itself needs no excursion: everything central is walkable from the ship. Portofino works independently on a normal call if you leave early. The Cinque Terre is the case for a ship tour or boat excursion: the journey takes a large part of the day, the trains are crowded in season, and you cannot miss the ship.

dayPlan.intro: Genoa city day. Assumes docking at 08:00 on a Tuesday to Sunday (the Strada Nuova museums close on Mondays) and an aquarium ticket booked ahead.

steps.what: Walk to Piazza Principe (6 minutes) and take the metro to De Ferrari.
Piazza De Ferrari and the San Lorenzo cathedral (open 08:00–12:00 and 15:00–19:00, so go in now, before the midday closure), then the caruggi towards Via Garibaldi.
Musei di Strada Nuova on Via Garibaldi: Palazzo Rosso, Palazzo Bianco and Palazzo Tursi.
Lift up to Spianata Castelletto for the view over the port; your AMT ticket covers it.
Lunch in the old town: focaccia, farinata or the fried fish of the Sottoripa arcades.
Acquario di Genova at Porto Antico (allow two hours).
Walk back along the waterfront (about 20 minutes) or take the metro from San Giorgio to Principe.
Back on board, 60 minutes before all-aboard.

sights.name: Old town (caruggi) and Via San Lorenzo
sights.why: A dense grid of narrow lanes between the port and Piazza De Ferrari.
sights.tip: Go by day and keep to the busier lanes around San Lorenzo, Piazza Banchi and Via Garibaldi. The San Lorenzo cathedral is free and opens 08:00–12:00 and 15:00–19:00; it is closed at midday.

sights.name: Via Garibaldi and the Musei di Strada Nuova
sights.why: The UNESCO-listed Rolli palaces: Palazzo Rosso, Palazzo Bianco and Palazzo Doria Tursi, with Van Dyck, Rubens, Caravaggio and Paganini's violin.
sights.tip: Closed on Mondays. Open Tuesday to Friday 09:00–19:00, weekends 10:00–19:30. During the Rolli Days (16–18 October 2026) extra palaces open with booking.

sights.name: Acquario di Genova
sights.why: Genoa's large aquarium on the Porto Antico waterfront.
sights.cost: From €26 for a fixed-date ticket; Open Flexi from €38 (2026)
sights.tip: Prices rise closer to the date; buy early online. Open every day of the year; last entry is two hours before closing.

sights.name: Porto Antico and the Bigo
sights.why: The old harbour, with the Bigo panoramic lift and the Biosfera glass sphere.
sights.tip: The Pianeta Acquario combined ticket adds both to the aquarium.

sights.name: Spianata Castelletto
sights.why: A terrace above the old town with views over the roofs to the port, reached by a public lift.
sights.tip: Good last stop before walking down to the ship.

sights.name: Portofino
sights.why: A small harbour village on the Portofino promontory, reached via Santa Margherita Ligure.
sights.cost: Train fare plus €5.00 each way on bus 782 (2026)
sights.tip: Leave early; the bus and the village fill up in high season.

sights.name: Cinque Terre
sights.why: The five cliff villages between Levanto and La Spezia.
sights.cost: Train fare plus Cinque Terre fare or supplement (2026)
sights.tip: Only on a long call and early start. A ship tour removes the risk of missing the ship.

beaches.name: Santa Margherita Ligure
beaches.howToGetThere: Regional train from Piazza Principe or Brignole.
beaches.note: Genoa has no beach within walking distance of the terminal; combine a swim stop here with Portofino.

commonMistakes.fix: Principe station is 6 minutes on foot and the old town and aquarium are walkable.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using the €2.00 AMT ticket on the Portofino bus.
Planning the Strada Nuova museums on a Monday.
commonMistakes.fix: They close on Mondays. Do the old town, Porto Antico and the aquarium instead.

commonMistakes.mistake: Attempting the Cinque Terre on a short call.
commonMistakes.fix: The trains and crowds eat the day. Choose Portofino, or book the ship's tour.

commonMistakes.mistake: Leaving the aquarium ticket until the day.
commonMistakes.fix: Fixed-date tickets are cheaper the earlier you buy.

commonMistakes.mistake: Not validating train or bus tickets.
commonMistakes.fix: Stamp paper tickets before boarding trains and on AMT vehicles.

safety: Genoa is generally safe by day for visitors. The old town's lanes are narrow and dark; stay on the main routes around San Lorenzo, Via Garibaldi and Porto Antico, and avoid empty side lanes after dark. Watch for pickpockets on crowded trains to the Riviera and at Principe and Brignole. Traffic on the waterfront road is heavy; cross at lights.
scams: Third-party resellers charging more for aquarium tickets than the official site. Buy on acquariodigenova.it, where earlier purchase is cheaper.
Pickpocketing on crowded Riviera trains and in Portofino and Cinque Terre crowds. Keep bags closed and in front.
Paper train and bus tickets that are not validated are treated as no ticket by inspectors. Always stamp before travel.
accessibility: The Ponte dei Mille terminal has lifts and escalators across its levels. Request assistance from Stazioni Marittime or your cruise line at least 48 hours ahead, and arrange any taxi or private car access to the quay in advance. The covered walk to Principe is level. The old town has narrow lanes, cobbles and steps; Porto Antico and the aquarium are the easiest areas. Genoa's lifts, such as the Castelletto lift, help with the hills. Regional trains to Portofino often have steps.
rainyDay: The aquarium is the obvious wet-weather choice, and the Musei di Strada Nuova and Palazzo Reale take a morning (both closed on Mondays). The Sottoripa arcades along the old harbour are covered. Portofino and the Cinque Terre are not worth it in heavy rain, and boats may be cancelled.
crowdTips: Genoa is a turnaround port, so embarkation days bring luggage queues and coaches at the terminal. The aquarium is busiest late morning and at weekends. Portofino and the Cinque Terre are crowded from late morning in high season, and trains between Levanto and La Spezia are packed. The Rolli Days (16–18 October 2026) bring extra visitors to Via Garibaldi; booking is required for the palaces.

faqs.q: Is Genoa cruise port walkable to the old town?
faqs.a: Yes. The terminal is about 1 km from the centre. Principe station is 6 minutes on foot and the aquarium about 20 minutes along the waterfront.
No. Ships berth at the Ponte dei Mille or Ponte Andrea Doria terminals.

faqs.q: How do I get from Genoa cruise port to Portofino?
faqs.a: Walk to Piazza Principe, take a regional train to Santa Margherita Ligure (about 26–60 minutes), then AMT bus 782, which costs €5.00 a ride (2026). In season, boats also run from Santa Margherita and from Genoa's Porto Antico.

faqs.q: Can I visit the Cinque Terre from Genoa on a cruise stop?
faqs.a: Only on a long call. The fastest trains take just under an hour to Monterosso, regionals longer, and a Cinque Terre fare or supplement applies until 1 November 2026. A ship tour is the safer choice.

faqs.q: How much is public transport in Genoa?
faqs.a: An AMT ordinary ticket costs €2.00 and is valid for 110 minutes on buses and the metro, including the Zecca–Righi funicular (2026).

faqs.q: What can I do in Genoa in one day from a cruise ship?
faqs.a: Walk the old town and Via Garibaldi, see the Strada Nuova palaces, take the lift to Spianata Castelletto, eat focaccia and farinata, and finish at the aquarium in Porto Antico.

faqs.q: Is Genoa safe for cruise passengers?
faqs.a: Yes by day with normal care. Stick to the busier lanes in the old town and watch for pickpockets on trains and in crowds.

faqs.q: Are there beaches near Genoa cruise port?
faqs.a: Not within walking distance. The nearest easy option is Santa Margherita Ligure, on the way to Portofino, by regional train.
